entries.title: Market Holidays
entries.notes: The exchange's own publication (page "Update : Feb. 06, 2026"). States the standing rule: "JPX markets are closed on Saturdays, Sundays, national holidays, and on the dates indicated below", where the dates indicated are Jan. 2, Jan. 3 and Dec. 31 every year. Also states the observance rule ("National holidays that fall on a Sunday are observed on the closest following day that is not a national holiday") and flags 2026-09-22 as a holiday "in accordance with Rule 3, Paragraph 3 of Act on National Holidays".

entries.title: Market Holidays (archived editions)
entries.publisher: Japan Exchange Group, via the Internet Archive
entries.notes: Earlier editions of the same JPX page. Jan. 2, Jan. 3 and Dec. 31 are listed as "Market Holiday" in every edition, including years in which they fall on a weekend. Source for the Olympic-year moves as JPX published them and for the 2019 imperial-transition holidays.

entries.title: 昭和30年（1955年）から令和9年（2027年）国民の祝日（csv形式）
entries.publisher: 内閣府 (Cabinet Office, Government of Japan)
entries.notes: Machine-readable list of every 国民の祝日 and every 休日 (both substitute holidays under Art. 3(2) and citizens' holidays under Art. 3(3)). The authoritative date list for everything statutory, including the Vernal and Autumnal Equinox dates.

entries.title: 「国民の祝日」について
entries.publisher: 内閣府 (Cabinet Office, Government of Japan)
entries.notes: Text of 国民の祝日に関する法律 (Act No. 178 of 1948): Art. 2 (the sixteen holidays and their rules, including the "Happy Monday" ones), Art. 3(2) (substitute holiday), Art. 3(3) (citizens' holiday), the note that the two equinox days are fixed annually by the National Astronomical Observatory in the February *kanpō* of the preceding year, and the table of the 2020/2021 Olympic moves of Marine Day, Sports Day and Mountain Day.

entries.title: The Failure of Equity Trading System on October 1, 2020
entries.publisher: Tokyo Stock Exchange, Inc. / Japan Exchange Group
entries.notes: "a failure occurred in the arrowhead cash equity trading system … which made it impossible to start trading and meant TSE was unable to provide opportunities for trading for the entire day". The basis for the single unscheduled full-day closure in coverage.

entries.title: 統計月報 2014年12月 1-1 内国株式総括表 (Monthly Statistics Report, Key Statistics for Domestic Stocks)
entries.publisher: Japan Exchange Group / Tokyo Stock Exchange
entries.notes: The exchange's own annual trading-day counts (立会日数): 2010 245, 2011 245, 2012 248, 2013 245, 2014 244, each equal to the modelled schedule month by month. 2011 has no lost session: trading continued through the March 2011 earthquake (tse-statement-2011-03-14).

entries.title: Monthly Statistics Report January 2016, Key Statistics for Domestic Stocks
entries.publisher: Japan Exchange Group / Tokyo Stock Exchange
entries.notes: Annual trading days 2011-2015 (2015: 244), equal to the modelled schedule.

entries.title: 統計月報 2019年8月 (Monthly Statistics Report, August 2019)
entries.publisher: Japan Exchange Group / Tokyo Stock Exchange
entries.notes: Annual trading days 2014-2018 (2016 245, 2017 247, 2018 245), equal to the modelled schedule.

entries.title: Monthly Statistics Report August 2026, Key Statistics for Domestic Stocks
entries.publisher: Japan Exchange Group / Tokyo Stock Exchange
entries.notes: Annual trading days 2021 245, 2022 244, 2023 246, 2024 245, 2025 243 and monthly counts to August 2026 (19, 18, 21, 21, 18, 22, 22, 20 for January-August 2026), each equal to the modelled schedule. Note that JPX counts the 1 October 2020 all-day suspension as a trading day (its 2020 count of 243 includes it), so these statistics verify the scheduled closures; the absence of other unscheduled suspensions rests on the exchange's news releases (jpx-system-failure-2020 is the only one in coverage) and on contemporaneous press.

entries.title: Trading Overview in Year 2020 & December 2020, Reference (TSE)
entries.publisher: Japan Exchange Group / Tokyo Stock Exchange
entries.notes: "(No. of Trading Days: 243)" for 2020 and the daily averages divide exactly by 243, the scheduled count: the exchange counts the 1 October 2020 suspension as a trading day. The 2013 and 2015-2025 reference sheets give the other years (2019 241; 2024 245; 2025 243).

entries.title: Tokyo Stock Exchange statement regarding the Tohoku district - off the Pacific Ocean earthquake (14 March 2011)
entries.publisher: Tokyo Stock Exchange (republished by Mondo Visione)
entries.notes: "Today TSE will operate regular trading sessions for stocks, futures, options, and other listed products." Trading continued every scheduled day after the 11 March 2011 earthquake.

entries.title: Partial Connection Failure in the Equity Trading System (arrowhead), 9 October 2018, and the report of 23 October 2018
entries.notes: "Trading is conducted as usual"; the report states the exchange "allowed trading for all issues according to the normal trading schedule". A partial connectivity failure, not a closure.
